summary: orderly-plugin-liquidity-heatmap postinstall performs GitHub Actions CI reconnaissance and OIDC probe
details: Package advertises an Orderly orderbook liquidity-heatmap plugin, but the shipped main (`dist/index.js`) exports a no-op `registerLiquidityHeatmapPlugin` that returns an empty function. The only substantive code in the tarball is a postinstall script gated on `CI && GITHUB_WORKSPACE` that collects a targeting profile of the GitHub Actions runner: host/user, repo and workflow identity, enumerated `GITHUB_*` / `ACTIONS_*` / `RUNNER_*` environment variable names, `GITHUB_TOKEN` presence and length, `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and token presence, npm registry, egress reachability to github and npm, and installed tool versions. The script actively exercises the runner's OIDC minting capability by curling `${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=api.github.com` with the runner's `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` as a bearer. The collected JSON snapshot is written to `heatmap-setup-report.json` in the repo workspace, appended in full to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and summarized through a `::notice::[liquidity-heatmap]...` log line, each of which is readable through the public GitHub workflow API — a side channel that externalizes the reconnaissance without a direct outbound POST. The stub implementation, mismatched README, CI-only gating, OIDC probe, and workflow-summary exfiltration together form a targeted dependency-confusion / CI reconnaissance payload against installers whose builds resolve this name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
